A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGDA study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and experimental and proof appendices. Content can be matched across reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original MGDA experiments on Cityscapes and NYU-v2, runtime comparisons, and measurements relating gradient norms to local smoothness.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds MoCo-warm-start results on Cityscapes and NYU-v2 in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: v5 applies the warm-start procedure to MoCo and evaluates the resulting MoCo-warm start in Appendix B.3. This is a limited procedural extension; the original MGDA, stochastic double-sampling, and MGDA-FA algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Cityscapes segmentation and depth estimation, and NYU-v2 segmentation, depth, and surface normals. The added MoCo experiments use this existing coverage without introducing another dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v5 adds dedicated comparisons between MoCo and its warm-start variant in Tables 6–7, extending the evaluated method variants. The comparator membership in the original MGDA benchmark tables and the MGDA-FA runtime comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: No existing split, metric, training budget, or testing rule is revised. The added MoCo comparisons use the retained benchmarks and metrics; the newly specified NYU-v2 settings document an existing experiment rather than establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 tests whether warm start also benefits another optimizer, comparing MoCo with and without warm start on both retained datasets. The existing gradient-smoothness analysis and MGDA-versus-MGDA-FA efficiency comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 changes MGDA-warm start's Cityscapes aggregate score from 3.93 to 3.93±1.19, introducing uncertainty reporting for that result. The meaning of ±1.19 and the number of runs or seeds are not specified, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: New Tables 6–7 report MoCo-warm-start aggregate scores of 7.32 versus MoCo's 9.90 on Cityscapes, and -0.88 versus 0.16 on NYU-v2, alongside task-level results. All original benchmark means and runtime values are retained.

T1.justification: v5 revises parameter conditions in Theorem 2 and the appendix theorems, expands and corrects Corollary 1's proof, and repairs factors in the fast-approximation and stochastic derivations, including remainder scaling and minibatch bounds. These are substantive local corrections within the retained assumptions, theorem framework, and advertised convergence rates.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: convergence under generalized smoothness, average and iteration-wise conflict-avoidance guarantees, the same sample-complexity rates, and efficient MGDA-FA. The added MoCo evidence supports the existing suggestion that warm start can benefit other algorithms.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly acknowledges that fast approximation can introduce substantial weight-update errors and that its stochastic convergence analysis is unavailable. It suggests FAMO's logarithmic technique as a possible improvement, without reporting its adoption. Appendix B.3 also interprets the new MoCo results as supporting warm-start transferability.

D1.justification: v5 newly documents NYU-v2 training details, including 200 SGD epochs, batch size 2, last-ten-epoch averaging, the hyperparameter search, and the selected learning rate of 0.0001. It also supplies a link to prior work's code for the smoothness illustration. Existing Cityscapes settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained, but v5 revises MoDo's reported iteration-wise complexity from O(ϵ^-16) to O(ϵ^-12) and distinguishes its CA weight-distance guarantee in Section 2.4. Table 1 changes SMG's assumption entry and adds sample-complexity comparisons; Appendix B.3 newly states that warm-started MoDo recovers the proposed algorithm.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v5 adds a notation-summary appendix and acknowledgments, shifts appendix lettering, adopts author–year citations and conference headers, and makes localized explanatory and wording edits.

P2.justification: v5 adds the notation table and two MoCo comparison tables, adds a complexity column to Table 1, and reflows the document into the ICLR format. The existing plots are unchanged, and the runtime table is retained as Table 5 rather than Table 4.

improvement.justification: v5 improves checkability through localized mathematical repairs and previously missing NYU-v2 implementation details. The MoCo comparisons provide direct support for warm-start transferability, while the new MGDA-FA caveats better explain its existing accuracy–speed tradeoff. These are useful but limited gains; the newly added uncertainty value remains inadequately defined.
